description: the crescent pocket of blend/cusp-pocket-fillet (the sliver between the walls void), both floor arcs concave and filleted at r 0.1 together: the stripes add material and meet on their own section from the floor's contact down to the spine one radius above the floor, which is cut there; the cusp vertex goes and no face is added (the mutual trim, ADR-0084). Held to a second kernel's record (ADR-0073)

analytic.counts_differ: Open CASCADE adds a thirteenth face, a B-spline corner patch from the ball at the offsets' meeting to the cusp vertex, which it keeps (19 / 29 / 13). The two concave stripes need none: each is its edge's exact rolling-ball blend, and run on they meet on their own intersection from the floor's contact to the spine at the radius above the floor, which cuts the spine and removes the cusp vertex (17 / 26 / 12). The second kernel builds exactly that (ADR-0084)
analytic.measure_differs: Open CASCADE's corner patch is an approximation that misses its own neighbours by its tolerance there, so its volume and area differ from the exact mutual trim's beyond its own bound on the patch (ADR-0084 as amended, tools/oracle/cusp_corner_second.py). The second kernel's volume and area, in second_oracle.json, agree with Open CASCADE's fuse of its own two single-edge fillets to 2.9e-6 of the body at worst, so the record is the exact mutual trim and not a third fit (ADR-0073, ADR-0084)

occt_step_refused.why: Open CASCADE's corner patch misses its own neighbours by up to its tolerance there (analytic.measure_differs): its own STEP writes the patch's boundary with #435 5.6e-3 off where the faces it meets put it, past the reader's cap of 3.7e-3 for a part this size, and closing it would move geometry. The file describes the oracle's patch, not a solid closed at the reader's tolerances; Arris's own STEP is still read back by Open CASCADE and compared
